steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Job production: one-off, unique products made to customer specification (e.g. custom wedding cake). High quality, high price, but slow and labour-intensive. | Key Fact: Batch production: groups of identical products made together (e.g. bakery making 50 loaves). Allows some variety but requires cleaning/resetting between batches. | Key Fact: Flow (mass) production: continuous, standardised production on an assembly line (e.g. car manufacturing). High volume, low unit cost, but high set-up costs and inflexible. | Key Fact: Productivity measures output per unit of input: labour productivity = output / number of workers. Higher productivity means lower unit costs and greater competitiveness.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Compare job production and flow production, giving one advantage and one disadvantage of each. | Explain how lean production can reduce a business's costs. | Evaluate which production method a furniture maker should use if they want to expand from bespoke to selling online nationwide.
